chapter: Ben Webster and Jim and Andy's
title: Jim and Andy's as a home away from home; Sonny
summary: Cook, loans, resident thief and prostitute, and the day Sonny took his daughter to Carnegie Hall.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: It was like a home away from home. They had a wonderful cook. You could go in there at any hour and know you're going to see a friend. If you're lonesome, you wanted to hang out, just talk, they didn't hustle you for drinks. You could sit there and have a coke, nurse it all night.
You could leave your instrument and your coat for weeks on end.
They would lend you money. They had a resident thief and a resident prostitute.
Absolutely. What was her name, Marge?

Sonny, yeah. Anything you'd need. Yeah, Sonny was a nice guy. My wife was furious at me because one night I had some tickets to a Duke Ellington concert and I brought my daughter in for dinner. And all of a sudden I had to stay later, so I said, 'Sonny, will you take my daughter to Carnegie Hall?' And my wife said, 'who's that man who brought Anne to Carnegie Hall?' I said, Sonny. She said, 'Sonny's a
thief?" I said, yeah. She said, "you sent your daughter to Carnegie Hall with a thief?" I said, he's a nice guy, you know. I don't know he's a thief; just people say he's a thief.

It's like that story about the writer Bemelmans he used to have this babysitter who was a child kidnapper. And he said, how could you leave your child with this known criminal? He said, I know that every policeman in Paris is watching him. I know she's as safe as she could possibly be. I figured with Sonny, my daughter's safe, all the cops had an eye on him.
